# `silk/net/resolver_native`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The native provider of the `Resolver` effect, with the `getaddrinfo` function of the system.

## When to use
Provide [`NativeSystemResolver`](#NativeSystemResolver) for `Resolver` in a native program when a blocking lookup is
acceptable. Code that resolves uses `silk.net.resolver`, so a test can provide a fake.

## Details
A host name without a deadline makes one `getaddrinfo` call with the name as written, so names in
the hosts file, such as `localhost`, resolve. The result is copied, and the list of the system is
freed one time, also on errors. Numeric hosts do not call the provider.

## Errors
`ResolverError` if the host is not found, has no address of the selected family, or the lookup
fails. A host name with a deadline fails with `DeadlineUnsupported`.

## Gotchas
- A host name with a deadline fails with `DeadlineUnsupported` before the lookup. After
  `getaddrinfo` starts, it cannot be cancelled or limited in time or memory.
- The lookup blocks the thread. It does not let another fiber run.
- [`NativeSystemResolver.make`](#NativeSystemResolver.impl.make) fails to compile on targets other than Darwin on aarch64, and
  Linux with GNU libc on x86_64 or aarch64.

## Examples
### Use the system resolver
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.system.monotonic_clock { MonotonicClock }
import silk.net.resolver_native { NativeSystemResolver }
import silk.net.address { AddressError, Host, Port }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.system.monotonic_clock_native { OsMonotonicClock }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.net.resolver { FamilySelection, ResolveRequest, ResolvedEndpoints, Resolver, ResolverError }
import silk.system.system_clock { Instant, SystemClock }

fn request(name: string, deadline: Option<Instant>) -> Option<ResolveRequest> {
  let host = match Host.parse(name) {
    Result<Host, AddressError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<Host, AddressError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return Option<ResolveRequest>.none()
    }
  }
  return match ResolveRequest.make(host, Port.fromU16(443), FamilySelection.Any, 8, move deadline) {
    Result<ResolveRequest, ResolverError>.Success { value } => Option<ResolveRequest>.some(
      move value
    )
    Result<ResolveRequest, ResolverError>.Failure { error: _ } => Option<ResolveRequest>.none()
  }
}

// Returns the number of endpoints of `name`. It blocks until the system lookup ends.
effect fn countEndpoints(name: string) -> usize
  ! ResolverError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Resolver | &mut MonotonicClock | &mut Allocator {
  let lookup = match request(name, Option<Instant>.none()) {
    Option.Some { value } => move value
    Option.None => {
      return 0
    }
  }
  let endpoints = run Resolver.resolve(&lookup)
  return ResolvedEndpoints.length(&endpoints)
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut resolver = NativeSystemResolver.make()
  let mut clock = OsMonotonicClock.make()

  // A host name with a deadline fails before the lookup starts.
  let limited = match request("example.com", Option<Instant>.some(SystemClock.make(1, 0))) {
    Option.Some { value } => move value
    Option.None => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let attempted = run Effect.result(Resolver.resolve(&limited))
    |> Effect.provideMut<Resolver>(&mut resolver)
    |> Effect.provideMut<MonotonicClock>(&mut clock)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  return match move attempted {
    Result.Success { value: _ } => 1
    Result.Failure { error } => match move error {
      ResolverError.DeadlineUnsupported => 0
      _ => 1
    }
  }
}
```

The native `Resolver` provider, with the `getaddrinfo` function of the system. It has no state.
